sounds.title: Sounds
sounds.hint: Your own sounds and music. You can enter the ID (e.g. namespace:block.ruby.place) anywhere a sound is expected – for block sounds, doors or /playsound, for example. “Jukebox Playable” turns the sound into a music disc.{target, select, nexo { Note: the exported sounds.yml replaces an existing file on the server.} other { Players hear new music discs after they rejoin. If an item plays a new music disc, restart the server once.}}
sounds.dropSubtitle: Each file becomes its own sound. Add more variants (played at random) inside the sound.
sounds.notOgg: “{name}” is not an OGG file. Minecraft only plays .ogg (convert it with Audacity, for example).
sounds.createDiscHint: A new item with the “Jukebox Playable” component for this song.
sounds.discCreated: Music disc item created – you can still add a model or texture.
sounds.weightHelp: How often this sound is picked compared to the other entries of the event, default 1
sounds.referenceHelp: Another sound event this sound plays (optional). Nexo then plays only that event, without the files.
sounds.preloadHint: (load with the pack, not when first played)
sounds.replaceHint: (replace the vanilla sound with this name; without files it goes silent)
sounds.jukeboxDocs: {target, select, craftengine {Jukebox songs in the CraftEngine wiki} other {Music discs in the Nexo docs}}
sounds.noFiles: No files yet. A sound without files replaces or references another sound.
sounds.durationMissing: Enter how long the song plays, e.g. 2m 30s.

paintings.title: Paintings
paintings.hint: Your own pictures to hang up.{target, select, nexo { From Minecraft 1.21.5 on, Nexo generates the required datapack. New paintings are only registered after a server restart – in the test server, use “Restart”. The exported paintings.yml replaces an existing file on the server.} other { Players see new paintings after they rejoin.}}
paintings.dropSubtitle: 16 pixels per block, e.g. 32×16 for a painting of 2×1 blocks. For animations, stack the frames vertically.
paintings.idHelp: Name of the painting, used in its key
paintings.randomPlaceHint: (also chosen at random when hanging normal paintings)
paintings.createItemHint: An item with material PAINTING that hangs exactly this painting.

dialogs.title: Dialogs
dialogs.hint: Dialog screens of Minecraft 1.21.6+: a title, text and items, inputs and buttons that run commands or open other dialogs. Each dialog becomes its own file in dialogs/; Nexo registers it as nexo:'<'id>. New dialogs need a server restart.
dialogs.idHelp: File name of the dialog, used in its key nexo:'<'id>

multipack.title: Multipack
multipack.hint: Template packs are resource packs Nexo sends along with the main pack. Put each one into plugins/Nexo/pack/template_packs/'<'id> on the server; the export only writes multipack.yml. Players toggle optional templates with /nexo multipack.

glyphs.title: Glyphs
glyphs.referenceGlyphHelp: Points to a cell of a multi-bitmap glyph
glyphs.hint: Glyphs are custom characters for chat, lore, item names, titles and GUIs. Use them anywhere with {tag}, e.g. in an item's lore.
glyphs.dropTitle: Drop PNG or GIF files here
glyphs.dropSubtitle: Each file becomes its own glyph – e.g. emojis (8×8) or GUI backgrounds (up to 256×256)
glyphs.notImage: “{name}” is not a PNG or GIF.
glyphs.idHelp: Name of the glyph, used in the tag
glyphs.permissionHelp: Permission needed to use the glyph (optional)
glyphs.sizeHelp: Height = size in game (chat text is 8 high). Ascent shifts the glyph up and must not be larger than the height. Split images over 256×256 into rows/columns.
glyphs.largeNoPreview: Large glyph (e.g. GUI) – no chat preview.
glyphs.charHelp: A fixed character for the glyph (optional, otherwise one is picked automatically)
glyphs.shadowHelp: Text shadow color of the glyph (optional, otherwise Glyphs.default_shadow in settings.yml)
glyphs.templateHelp: Another glyph whose settings this glyph takes over (optional)
glyphs.gifTypeHelp: How the animation is made: core shader or sprite sheet
glyphs.emojiHint: What a chat shortcut of this glyph turns into. Empty fields use CraftEngine’s default.
glyphs.emojiContentHelp: MiniMessage; '<'arg:emoji> is the image, '<'arg:keyword> the shortcut that was typed

testServer.connectLater: Once the server runs: Minecraft {version} → Multiplayer → Direct Connection → <mono>{address}</mono>

testServer.openFolder: Open the server folder in Explorer

pack.resendHint: Send the resource pack to {player} again
pack.enterName: Please enter your Minecraft name below

sync.auto: Transfer automatically when I change something
sync.autoHint: New items, changed models and properties are in the game after a few seconds – the resource pack is sent again.

sync.projectErrors: The project has {count, plural, one {# error} other {# errors}} (see “Export”) – affected items may not work in game.

console.title: Console
console.placeholderNoItems: e.g. gamemode creative {player}  ·  time set day

setup.title: Setup
setup.lockedDescription: Stop the server to change the version, memory, ports or world.
setup.description: Downloaded automatically on the first start (Paper, Java if needed).
setup.jarHelp: Your {plugin} JAR{target, select, nexo { (e.g. from Polymart)} other {}}. It is only copied into the local test server.
setup.jarSelected: {plugin} {version} will be used in the test server.
setup.jarDownloadHelp: Downloads {plugin} from Modrinth for the chosen Minecraft version. You can also choose a JAR yourself, for example a premium build. It is only copied into the local test server.
setup.versionMismatch: The project is set to {version} – ideally test with the same version, if available.
setup.versionHelp: Your Minecraft must have the same version.
setup.playerHelp: Gets OP rights and the items via “Give in test server”.
setup.portHelp: Default 25565 – choose another one if a different server already uses it.
setup.eulaHint: A Minecraft server may not be started without accepting it.
setup.packPortHelp: The plugin serves the resource pack on this port (default 8082).

setup.worldHelp: A flat creative world. Reset it if it no longer loads or you want a clean one.
setup.resetWorldMessage: The test server’s world is deleted, including everything built in it. A new flat world is created on the next start.
setup.worldResetDone: World deleted – a new one is created on the next start.
setup.noPlugin: Without the {plugin} plugin the server starts, but your items won't be loaded.

lootSources.title: Loot sources
lootSources.hint: A loot source adds a loot table to a vanilla loot event: breaking a block, killing a mob, opening a chest, fishing and more. With overwrite it replaces the vanilla items or experience.

templates.title: Templates
templates.hint: A template is a piece of config with placeholders for arguments. Blocks use one in their settings, items for the whole item, loot tables and events too. CraftEngine's default templates (default:…) are always there.
templates.defaultsHint: Every block, item and furniture can use these. Required arguments are marked with *.

globalVariables.title: Global variables
globalVariables.hint: A global variable is a MiniMessage text that CraftEngine puts in wherever a text says '<'global:name>: in item names, lore and more. The previews in the item editor show it too.

attributes.title: Attributes
attributes.hint: CraftEngine's attribute system is experimental and only runs with attribute.enable: true in its config.yml, which it reads on startup. The test server switches it on for a project that uses attributes; restart it after adding the first one.

definitions.title: Attributes
definitions.hint: Custom values such as strength or critical chance, each with a base value and limits. Items change them in their settings (Custom Attribute Modifiers).

operations.title: Operations
operations.hint: Your own ways to apply a modifier, besides add_value, add_multiplied_base and add_multiplied_total.

equipmentSets.title: Equipment sets
equipmentSets.hint: Bonuses for wearing several pieces of a set. Items become pieces in their settings (Equipment Set Piece).

damageRules.title: Damage rules
damageRules.hint: Formulas that compute the damage of a damage type from the attributes of attacker and victim.

translations.title: Translations
translations.hint: Item names with translations and the names of custom blocks go into the language files by themselves. Here you add your own keys: lang keys the client translates (use them as '<'lang:key>), and server translations CraftEngine fills in itself ('<'l10n:key> in each player's language, '<'i18n:key> in the server's).

lang.title: Lang keys (resource pack)
lang.hint: Written into the resource pack's language files. The language all writes a key into every language; block_name:namespace:id names a custom block. Changes need a resource pack reload.

server.title: Server translations
server.hint: Read on the server, so changes need no resource pack reload. A language without a country (en) also covers its regions.

categories.title: Categories
categories.hint: A category groups items in CraftEngine's /ce item browser. It lists items and other categories, matches item ids by a regular expression or takes all items. An item can also add itself with its Category property.
categories.fromFoldersOn: The export also writes a category for each folder (project setting); one of yours with the same id replaces it.
categories.fromFoldersOff: The project setting for one category per folder is off, so only these categories are written.

worldgen.title: Worldgen features
worldgen.hint: A configured feature is what generates, e.g. the shape of a tree; a placed feature is where and how often. Write the YAML with misode's datapack generator (set to your server's version and YAML output) and use your custom block ids in it.

configured.title: Configured features
configured.hint: Saplings grow these. A placed feature names one or holds its own.

placed.title: Placed features
placed.hint: These generate in the world. Grass blocks grow these with bone meal.

atlases.title: Atlases
atlases.hint: Most packs need no atlas: CraftEngine repairs the common block and item atlas cases itself. Add one to put textures into a vanilla atlas or build a custom sprite atlas.

pack.title: Pack
pack.hint: The namespace and description come from the project settings; set the rest of pack.yml here.

packYml.title: pack.yml
packYml.hint: Author and version show in CraftEngine. Subpacks are folders of the pack that load as packs of their own.

factories.title: Config factories
factories.hint: A config factory writes its blueprint once per instance, each time with that instance's arguments: e.g. a sofa item and recipe for every wool color.

scripts.title: Scripts
scripts.hint: Scripts go into the pack's script folder. js functions and conditions call their functions by the script id namespace:path; annotations like //@Subscribe and //@Task register event handlers and tasks. CraftEngine runs them only with scripting.js.enable: true in its config.yml; the test server switches it on.
